title: Weighted holdback experiments for staged variant adoption and pinned model swaps
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Background: When pinning customers to a model revision we currently support simple canary ramps and shadowing. For high-risk or cost-sensitive models (large context, new quantization profile) teams have asked for tighter experiment primitives that let us stage adoption with a small persistent holdback target and weighted exposures to validate model behavior over time.

Goal: Provide a repeatable experiment pattern that: 1) reduces blast radius for new pinned model swaps, 2) surfaces regressions in both quality and cost signals early, and 3) supports deterministic roll-forward / rollback policies. The pattern should be usable by product teams without deep infra changes and integrate with performance profile publishing so that pinned variants can carry cost/latency expectations.

Success metrics (sample):
- Detectable quality regressions flagged within first 48h for 95% of staged releases (measured by evaluation prompts + user metrics).
- Mean latency and token-cost deviations captured and visible within first 2k requests.
- Rollback automation trigger reduces impacted users by >90% compared to manual rollback for regression cases.

Scope: UX for creating "weighted holdback experiments" in Console, rollout orchestration hooks in control plane, small runtime changes to allow persistent holdback cohorts, telemetry wiring to new dashboard widgets, and a playbook for PM/SEs. Not included: major model registry redesign or new quota model changes.
acceptance_criteria: Console can create an experiment that pins X% of traffic to new_variant, Y% to baseline, and H% to holdback cohort
Control plane enforces weight splits and can persist cohort assignments across sessions
Telemetry dashboard shows per-cohort latency, cost-per-token, safety flag rate, and eval-set scoring within 24 hours of rollout
Automated rollback policy can be configured by threshold (latency or eval delta) and executed without manual intervention
Documentation (runbook) and templates exist for PMs to spin up experiments and interpret signals
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight cohort allocator in the control plane that supports deterministic hashing and sticky assignments by customer token/user-id
Expose an API field on pins for "experiment_config" that accepts weights and holdback percent; default holdback=1%
Runtime must support routing to a 'holdback' variant that uses existing baseline runtime path (no quantization changes) to minimize interpretability noise
Telemetry: publish cohort-tagged traces and token-level cost estimates to the existing console telemetry stream
Rollout policy: support both hard thresholds and rolling-window anomaly detection for safety signals
Trade-offs: heavier telemetry can increase cost and noise; initial iteration will sample traces at 10% and increase if signal is low

roll_forward_plan: Start with 0.5% holdback and 1% variant exposure for 24h synthetic + live traffic, increase to 5%/5% after 72h if all signals green. If evaluation delta > threshold or safety flags exceed configured rate, trigger automated rollback and notify on-call with pre-populated incident runbook link.
